ujjain.s: Ujjain is an ancient city in central India on the Shipra River, one of the seven sacred cities of Hinduism. It was a major commercial and administrative centre on routes linking northern India with the western coast.

ukiyo-e.s: Ukiyo-e, meaning 'pictures of the floating world', is a genre of Japanese woodblock prints and paintings that flourished from the seventeenth to the nineteenth centuries. It depicted actors, courtesans, landscapes and scenes of urban life.

ukraine.s: Ukraine is a country in eastern Europe whose fertile steppe lands have been contested by many powers. Much of it formed part of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, where the Khmelnytsky uprising of 1648 began the loss of eastern territories to Russia.

ulama.s: The ulama are the community of Muslim religious scholars, trained in Islamic law, theology and scripture. They staffed courts, schools and mosques and often mediated between rulers and subjects.

ulpian.s: Ulpian was a Roman jurist of the early third century CE and one of the most influential legal writers in Roman history. He served as praetorian prefect under Severus Alexander and was killed by the Praetorian Guard.

ulugh-beg.s: Ulugh Beg was a Timurid ruler and astronomer, a grandson of Timur, who governed Samarkand for decades and died in 1449. He built a great observatory and madrasa in Samarkand and sponsored astronomical tables of remarkable accuracy.

ulugh-beg-observatory.s: The Ulugh Beg Observatory was an astronomical observatory built in Samarkand in the 1420s by the Timurid ruler Ulugh Beg. Its huge meridian arc allowed precise measurements, and the astronomers who worked there produced a star catalogue and astronomical tables.

umar-din.s: Umar Din was a sultan of the Walashma dynasty in the Adal Sultanate in the sixteenth century. The Adal Sultanate profile notes that Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi held real power as leader of the jihad against Christian Ethiopia while maintaining a nominal Walashma sultan,…

umar-ibn-al-khattab.s: Umar ibn al-Khattab was the second caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate, ruling from 634 to 644 CE. Under his leadership Muslim armies conquered Syria, Iraq, Egypt and much of Iran, and he established key institutions such as the diwan for paying soldiers and garrison cities.

umayyad-caliphate.s: The Umayyad Caliphate was the second Islamic caliphate, ruled by the Umayyad family from Damascus from 661 to 750 CE. It expanded Muslim rule from Iberia and North Africa to Central Asia and the Indus valley, and established Arabic as the language of administration.

umayyad-conquest-of-hispania.s: The Umayyad conquest of Hispania was the Muslim conquest of most of the Iberian Peninsula beginning in 711 CE. Forces led by Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed from North Africa and defeated the Visigothic king Roderic, and within a few years most of the peninsula was under Umayyad control.

umayyad-conquest-of-sind.s: The Umayyad conquest of Sind was the campaign of 711 CE in which forces led by Muhammad ibn Qasim conquered Sind, in the lower Indus valley in present-day Pakistan. It brought the region under the Umayyad Caliphate and marked the eastern limit of early Arab expansion into…

unequal-treaties.s: Unequal treaties is a term for agreements imposed on East Asian states by Western powers in the nineteenth century, granting privileges such as extraterritoriality, fixed tariffs and treaty ports. China and Japan were both subject to them.

unesco-world-heritage-site.s: A UNESCO World Heritage Site is a place recognised by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization as having outstanding cultural or natural value. The Elamite Confederation profile notes that the Chogha Zanbil ziggurat built under Untash-Napirisha…

union-of-krewo.s: The Union of Krewo was an agreement of 1385 under which Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania agreed to accept Catholic Christianity and marry Queen Jadwiga of Poland, becoming King of Poland. It created a personal union between Poland and Lithuania.

union-of-lublin.s: The Union of Lublin was the agreement of 1569 that transformed the personal union of Poland and Lithuania into a single state, the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. The two parts retained separate administrations and armies but shared an elected monarch and a common Sejm.

united-nations.s: The United Nations is an international organisation founded in 1945 to maintain peace and promote cooperation among states, with its headquarters in New York. The Hittite Empire profile notes that a reproduction of the Egyptian–Hittite peace treaty of Kadesh hangs at the…

united-states.s: The United States is a federal republic in North America that became independent from Britain in 1776 and grew into a major world power. It defeated the Spanish Empire in 1898, acquiring Spain's remaining overseas colonies, and was the principal adversary of the Empire of…

universal-suffrage.s: Universal suffrage is the right of all adult citizens to vote, regardless of property, class or, in its full form, sex. The German Empire introduced universal male suffrage for elections to the Reichstag in 1871.

untash-napirisha.s: Untash-Napirisha was a king of Elam in the fourteenth century BCE. He built the religious complex of Chogha Zanbil near Susa, centred on a great ziggurat.

uparika.s: An uparika was a provincial governor in the Gupta Empire. The Gupta Empire profile explains that the empire was divided into provinces called bhuktis, each administered by an uparika, frequently a member of the royal family.

upemba-depression.s: The Upemba Depression is a low-lying basin of lakes, marshes and fertile land along the upper Lualaba River in the south-east of the present-day Democratic Republic of the Congo. Archaeological sites there show long continuous occupation.

upper-egypt.s: Upper Egypt is the southern part of Egypt, the narrow Nile Valley stretching from around Memphis southwards to the First Cataract at Aswan. It was home to Thebes, the religious centre of the New Kingdom.

upper-mesopotamia.s: Upper Mesopotamia is the northern part of the land between the Tigris and Euphrates, covering parts of present-day northern Iraq, north-eastern Syria and south-eastern Turkey. Rain-fed agriculture and trade routes supported cities such as Assur and Nineveh, making it the…

ur.s: Ur was an ancient Sumerian city in southern Mesopotamia, near the former course of the Euphrates in present-day Iraq. It reached its height as the capital of the Third Dynasty of Ur, or Neo-Sumerian Empire, under Ur-Nammu and his successors, who built its great ziggurat.

ural-mountains.s: The Ural Mountains are a north–south mountain range in Russia, traditionally regarded as the boundary between Europe and Asia. The Russian Empire profile notes that under Ivan IV Russian expansion crossed the Urals into Siberia, a process accelerated by Yermak Timofeyevich's…

urdu.s: Urdu is an Indo-Aryan language closely related to Hindi, written in a Perso-Arabic script and rich in Persian and Arabic vocabulary. It developed in northern India from the interaction of local speech with the Persian of the ruling elites.

urf.s: Urf is a term for customary law, and in the Safavid Empire it referred to the royal law administered through the Shah's courts. The Safavid Empire profile explains that while Shia judges applied religious law to personal status and family matters, urf handled criminal,…

ur-nammu.s: Ur-Nammu was the founder of the Third Dynasty of Ur, or Neo-Sumerian Empire, who established his rule around 2112 BCE after the collapse of the Akkadian Empire. He is credited with the Code of Ur-Nammu, one of the oldest known law codes, and with major building projects…

urshu.s: Urshu was an ancient city in northern Syria or south-eastern Anatolia, besieged by the Hittites during their early expansion. A Hittite text describing the siege provides rare detail on early siege warfare.

uruguay.s: Uruguay is a country in South America on the east bank of the Río de la Plata. In the early nineteenth century the territory, then known as the Cisplatine Province, was contested between Brazil and Argentina, and the costly war over it ended with Uruguayan independence in 1828.

uruk.s: Uruk was one of the oldest and largest cities of ancient Sumer, in southern Mesopotamia, and is associated with the early development of writing and urban life. It was the city of the legendary king Gilgamesh.

ur-zababa.s: Ur-Zababa was a king of the Sumerian city of Kish in the late third millennium BCE. According to tradition, the future Sargon of Akkad served as his cupbearer.

us-oil-embargo-against-japan.s: The US oil embargo against Japan was the cutting off of American oil exports to Japan in 1941, imposed in response to Japanese expansion in Indochina. The Empire of Japan profile notes that Japan imported approximately eighty percent of its oil from the United States.

usman-dan-fodio.s: Usman dan Fodio was a Fulani Islamic scholar and reformer who led a jihad against the Hausa kingdoms beginning in 1804 and founded the Sokoto Caliphate. His movement created one of the largest states in nineteenth-century Africa and inspired other reform movements across West…

uss-missouri.s: The USS Missouri was a United States Navy battleship of the Iowa class, commissioned during the Second World War. On 2 September 1945 the formal Japanese surrender was signed aboard it in Tokyo Bay.

uthman-ibn-affan.s: Uthman ibn Affan was the third caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate, ruling from 644 to 656 CE. His reign saw continued expansion and the compilation of a standard text of the Quran, but accusations of favouring his Umayyad kinsmen provoked growing discontent.

uyghurs.s: The Uyghurs are a Turkic people who founded a powerful khaganate on the Mongolian steppe in the mid-eighth century after overthrowing the Second Turkic Khaganate in alliance with others. The Uyghur Khaganate became a major ally of the Tang Dynasty before its collapse in 840.

uzama.s: The uzama were the hereditary noble chiefs of the Benin kingdom, who held significant power under the earlier Ogiso system. The Benin Empire profile describes how the Oba dynasty centralised royal authority against them, and how Oba Ewuare the Great removed the uzama chiefs'…

uzbekistan.s: Uzbekistan is a country in Central Asia covering much of historic Transoxiana, including the cities of Samarkand, Bukhara and Tashkent. It was the heartland of the Timurid Empire, whose capital was Samarkand, and an important part of the Chagatai Empire.

uzbeks.s: The Uzbeks are a Turkic people of Central Asia whose name derives from the nomadic confederation that formed in the fifteenth century. Under Muhammad Shaybani they conquered Transoxiana from the Timurids around 1500, ending Timurid rule there and driving Babur south.

uzun-hasan.s: Uzun Hasan was the ruler of the Aq Qoyunlu Turkmen confederation, who died in 1478. He built a powerful state in eastern Anatolia, Iraq and western Iran but was defeated by the Ottomans at Otlukbeli in 1473.

ui-neill.s: The Uí Néill were a group of Irish dynasties claiming descent from Niall of the Nine Hostages. The northern branches ruled Ailech and Tír Eoghain and Tír Chonaill, and the southern branches ruled Mide and Brega.

upper-burma.s: Upper Burma is the inland, northern part of Myanmar around the middle Irrawaddy, including the dry zone where Pagan, Ava and Mandalay stood. It was the heartland of most Burmese kingdoms, in contrast to the Mon country of Lower Burma.

upper-lusatia.s: Upper Lusatia is a historical region on the upper Spree and Neisse, centred on Bautzen and Görlitz, today divided between Germany and Poland. Settled by the Sorbs, it was long held by the Bohemian crown, while its six leading towns formed the Lusatian League in 1346.

union-of-utrecht.s: The Union of Utrecht was an alliance signed in January 1579 by the northern provinces of the Netherlands, led by Holland and Zeeland, to fight together against Spanish rule. It promised mutual defence and freedom of conscience.

upper-silesia.s: Upper Silesia is the south-eastern part of Silesia, on the upper Oder, today mostly in Poland with a part in the Czech Republic. In the Middle Ages it was divided among Piast duchies such as Opole, Racibórz, Bytom and Cieszyn, which came under the Bohemian crown.

uberto-pallavicino.s: Uberto Pallavicino was a Lombard nobleman and leader of the Ghibelline party, a supporter of Emperor Frederick II. From the 1250s he was lord of Cremona, Piacenza and other cities, and briefly of Milan.

udaybhan-singh.s: Udaybhan Singh was the last ruling Maharaj Rana of Dholpur, a Jat princely state in Rajputana, from 1911. He acceded to India in 1947, and in 1948 he became Rajpramukh of the Matsya Union, formed from Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur and Karauli, before it merged into Rajasthan in 1949.

uesugi-kagekatsu.s: Uesugi Kagekatsu was the adopted heir of Uesugi Kenshin, who won the succession war after Kenshin's death in 1578. Under Toyotomi Hideyoshi he was moved to Aizu with large holdings.

uesugi-kenshin.s: Uesugi Kenshin was a warlord of Echigo province in the Sengoku period, famous for his generalship and Buddhist devotion. He fought Takeda Shingen in five battles at Kawanakajima between 1553 and 1564 and campaigned repeatedly against the Later Hojo in the Kanto.

umar-ibn-hafsun.s: Umar ibn Hafsun was a muwallad rebel who led a long revolt against the Umayyad Emirate of Córdoba from his mountain fortress of Bobastro in southern al-Andalus. He drew support from converts and Christians, allied with other rebels such as the lords of Seville, and is said to…

umur-bey.s: Umur Bey was ruler of the Aydinid beylik in western Anatolia from 1334. From Smyrna his fleets raided the Aegean islands and Greek coasts, and he allied with the Byzantine John VI Kantakouzenos.

upper-march.s: The Upper March was the north-eastern frontier province of al-Andalus, facing the Franks and the Christian kingdoms of the Pyrenees, with its capital at Zaragoza. Local dynasties such as the Banu Qasi of Tudela and later the Tujibids dominated it.

ural-river.s: The Ural River, historically the Yaik, flows from the southern Ural Mountains to the Caspian Sea and is often taken as a boundary between Europe and Asia. Its steppes were grazing lands of the White Horde and the Nogai Horde, whose capital Saraychik stood on it.

united-states-declaration-of-independenc.s: The United States Declaration of Independence was adopted by the Second Continental Congress in Philadelphia on 4 July 1776. Drafted mainly by Thomas Jefferson, it announced that the thirteen American colonies were independent states no longer bound to Britain, listed…

ugyen-wangchuck.s: Ugyen Wangchuck was the first hereditary king of Bhutan, elected by an assembly of clergy, officials and leading families at Punakha in 1907. As penlop of Trongsa he defeated his rivals in the civil wars of the late 19th century and won British favour by helping the…

ukit-kan-lek-tok.s: Ukit Kan Le'k Tok' was a Maya king of Ek' Balam in north-eastern Yucatán who took power in 770 and made the city the capital of a regional kingdom, Talol. He died around 801 and was buried in the great Acropolis, in a tomb behind a stucco facade shaped as the jaws of a monster…

ulugh-muhammad.s: Ulugh Muhammad was a Chinggisid khan of the Golden Horde who, after losing power in the struggles of the early 15th century, moved to the middle Volga and around 1438 founded the Khanate of Kazan. He defeated and captured Vasily II of Moscow at Suzdal in 1445, the year he was…

umar-al-aqta.s: Umar al-Aqta was emir of Melitene, a frontier emirate on the upper Euphrates, from about 830 to 863 and one of the most dangerous Arab raiders of Byzantine Anatolia. Allied with the Paulicians of Tephrike, he sacked Amisos on the Black Sea in 863, but was trapped and killed…

umar-walasma.s: Umar Walasma was the founder of the Walashma dynasty and of the Sultanate of Ifat in the eastern highlands of Shewa, Ethiopia. Claiming Arab descent, he conquered the old Sultanate of Shewa in 1285 and absorbed it, creating a Muslim state on the trade routes between the…

umaru-dallaji.s: Umaru Dallaji was a Fulani scholar and follower of Usman dan Fodio who led the jihad in Katsina, capturing the city from its Hausa ruler in 1807. He became the first emir of Katsina within the Sokoto Caliphate, ruling until his death in 1835 and founding the Dallazawa dynasty.

united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-irel.n: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-irel.s: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland was the state created on 1 January 1801 by the Acts of Union, which merged the Kingdom of Great Britain and the Kingdom of Ireland under one parliament at Westminster. It ruled the largest empire of the 19th century.

united-states-military-government-of-the.n: United States Military Government of the Philippine Islands
united-states-military-government-of-the.s: The United States Military Government of the Philippine Islands was the American military administration of the Philippines from the capture of Manila in August 1898. Under a series of military governors it fought the Philippine–American War against the First Philippine Republic.

united-states-military-government-in-cub.n: United States Military Government in Cuba
united-states-military-government-in-cub.s: The United States Military Government in Cuba ruled the island from 1 January 1899, after Spain gave it up at the end of the Spanish–American War, until 20 May 1902. Under the governors John R.

upper-bavaria.s: Upper Bavaria is the southern and south-eastern part of Bavaria, around Munich, Ingolstadt and the Alpine foothills. It emerged as a separate duchy in the Wittelsbach partition of 1255, when Louis II the Strict received it with Munich as his residence, and the duchies of…

uzbek-khan.s: Uzbek Khan was khan of the Golden Horde from 1313 to 1341, the longest reign in its history. He made Islam the state religion, built mosques in the capital Sarai and kept close ties with Mamluk Egypt.

ugandan-bush-war.s: The Ugandan Bush War was the guerrilla war waged by Yoweri Museveni's National Resistance Army against the second government of Milton Obote and then the military regime of Tito Okello. Fighting centred on the Luwero Triangle north of Kampala, where many civilians were killed.

university-of-greifswald.s: The University of Greifswald is a university in the Baltic town of Greifswald in Pomerania, north-eastern Germany, founded in 1456 with the support of Duke Wartislaw IX and the burgomaster Heinrich Rubenow. It became Lutheran during the Reformation.

udai-singh-of-marwar.s: Udai Singh, known as Mota Raja, was the Rathore ruler of Marwar (Jodhpur) from 1583 to 1595, restored to his kingdom as a vassal of Akbar. His daughter married Prince Salim, the future Jahangir, and was the mother of Shah Jahan.

ubashi-khan.s: Ubashi Khan was the last khan of the Kalmyk Khanate on the lower Volga, ruling from 1761. Resenting Russian settlement, Cossack encroachment and interference in Kalmyk affairs, in January 1771 he led about 150,000 Kalmyks east across the Kazakh steppe towards Dzungaria.

udai-singh-of-dungarpur.s: Rawal Udai Singh was ruler of Vagad, with his capital at Dungarpur in southern Rajasthan, in the early 16th century. An ally of Rana Sanga of Mewar, he was killed fighting the Mughal emperor Babur at the Battle of Khanwa in 1527.

udai-singh-of-kaithal.s: Bhai Udai Singh was the last ruler of Kaithal, a Sikh chiefship of the Cis-Sutlej region in present-day Haryana that had accepted British protection in 1809. When he died childless in 1843, the British East India Company annexed most of the state as a lapsed territory and put…

udayana-warmadewa.s: Udayana Warmadewa was a king of Bali of the Warmadewa dynasty in the late 10th and early 11th centuries, ruling from the region of Bedulu. He married the Javanese princess Mahendradatta, and the royal couple issued joint charters.

udayana-of-vatsa.s: Udayana was a king of Vatsa, with its capital at Kaushambi on the Yamuna, in the 6th century BCE, a contemporary of the Buddha. Buddhist texts and Sanskrit drama make him a romantic hero: his capture by King Pradyota of Avanti and his elopement with Pradyota's daughter…

uesugi-harunori.s: Uesugi Harunori, also known as Uesugi Yōzan, was daimyo of the Yonezawa Domain in northern Japan from 1767 to 1785. Facing near bankruptcy, he cut expenses, encouraged sericulture, weaving, lacquer trees and carp ponds, reclaimed land and revived the domain school, the Kōjōkan.

uhtred-the-bold.s: Uhtred the Bold was earl of Bamburgh and, from about 1006, of all Northumbria until his death in 1016. He won fame by defeating a Scottish army besieging Durham in 1006 and was rewarded by King Æthelred the Unready, whose daughter he married.

ui-dunlainge.s: The Uí Dúnlainge were a dynasty of north Leinster, in the plains of modern Kildare, descended from Dúnlaing mac Énda Niada. From the 8th to the 11th century they held the kingship of Leinster almost without break, rotating it between three branches, the Uí Muiredaig, Uí…

ukrainian-soviet-republic.s: The Ukrainian Soviet Republic was a short-lived Bolshevik state proclaimed in March 1918 by merging the Ukrainian People's Republic of Soviets with the other Soviet republics set up in Ukraine, including those of Odessa and Donetsk–Krivoy Rog. Formed as German and…

ulick-de-burgh.s: Ulick de Burgh was the founder of the Clanricarde Burkes of south Galway. After the murder of his kinsman William Donn de Burgh, Earl of Ulster, in 1333, he seized the family's lands in southern Connacht and took the Gaelic title Mac William Uachtar, ruling from Loughrea.

ulick-fionn-burke.s: Ulick Fionn Burke was Mac William Uachtar, lord of Clanricarde in south Galway, from 1485 until his death in 1509. In 1504 he led an alliance with the O'Briens and other Gaelic lords against Gerald FitzGerald, 8th Earl of Kildare, the Lord Deputy of Ireland, and was heavily…

ulises-heureaux.s: Ulises Heureaux was a Dominican general and dictator who dominated the Dominican Republic from 1882 until his assassination in 1899. A hero of the War of Restoration against Spain and a leader of Gregorio Luperón's Blue Party, he became president in 1882 and ruled almost…

ulric-manfred-ii.s: Ulric Manfred II was margrave of Turin from about 1000 until his death in 1034, of the Arduinici family. He controlled the Alpine routes over the Mont Cenis and Mont Genèvre passes, extended the march across much of western Piedmont and founded monasteries, including San…

ulrich-duke-of-mecklenburg.s: Ulrich, Duke of Mecklenburg, was administrator of the Prince-Bishopric of Schwerin from 1550 and ruled Mecklenburg-Güstrow from 1555 until his death in 1603. A Lutheran prince, he introduced the Reformation in the bishopric, which in practice became an appanage of the…

ulugh-khan.s: Ulugh Khan was a general of the Delhi Sultanate and a brother of Sultan Alauddin Khalji. With Nusrat Khan he invaded Gujarat in 1299, sacking Anahilavada and the temple of Somnath and forcing the Vaghela king Karna to flee.

uluj-ali.s: Uluj Ali was an Italian-born Ottoman corsair and admiral, born in Calabria as Giovanni Dionigi Galeni and captured by Barbary corsairs as a young man. Converting to Islam, he rose to be beylerbey of Algiers from 1568.

umar-al-mutawakkil.s: Umar al-Mutawakkil was the last Aftasid ruler of the Taifa of Badajoz, from about 1067 until 1094, and a noted poet whose court attracted writers. Pressed by Alfonso VI of Castile and fearing the Almoravids, he ceded Lisbon, Sintra and Santarém to Castile in 1093 in return for…

umar-ibn-abd-al-aziz-al-habbari.s: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Habbari was the founder of the Habbari dynasty of Sindh. From an Arab family settled in the province since the conquest, he made himself ruler around 854 at al-Mansura, the provincial capital, as Abbasid authority weakened, while continuing to recognise…

umar-ibn-awad-al-quaiti.s: Umar ibn Awad al-Qu'aiti was the founder of the fortunes of the Qu'aiti family of Hadramawt in southern Arabia. A Yafa'i tribesman, he rose to high rank as a jamadar, or commander, of the Arab troops of the Nizam of Hyderabad in India.

umaru-nagwamatse.s: Umaru Nagwamatse was the founder of the Kontagora Emirate in western Nigeria. A son of the Sokoto caliph Abubakar Atiku and a grandson of Usman dan Fodio, he left Sokoto with followers and around 1859 began conquering lands among the Kamuku, Gbagyi and other peoples between…

umma-khan-v.s: Umma Khan V, called the Great, was khan of Avar in mountainous Dagestan from 1774 until his death in 1801, when the khanate was at the height of its power. He led raids deep into Georgia and Shirvan and received tribute and payments from neighbouring rulers, including the…

united-nations-general-assembly.s: The United Nations General Assembly is the main deliberative body of the United Nations, in which every member state has one vote. First meeting in London in January 1946, it debates international questions, approves the budget and admits members on the Security Council's…

united-nations-security-council.s: The United Nations Security Council is the organ of the United Nations responsible for international peace and security, with power to impose sanctions and authorise force by binding decisions. It has five permanent members with a veto, China, France, Russia (formerly the…

united-fruit-company.s: The United Fruit Company was an American corporation, founded in 1899, that dominated banana growing and trade in Central America and the Caribbean. Owning vast lands, railways and ports, it wielded great political influence, especially in Guatemala, where dictators such as…

united-republic-of-tanganyika-and-zanzib.n: United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar
united-republic-of-tanganyika-and-zanzib.s: The United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar was the union formed on 26 April 1964 by Tanganyika under Julius Nyerere and the People's Republic of Zanzibar under Abeid Karume, a few months after the Zanzibar Revolution. Zanzibar kept its own president and government for…

united-workers-party-saint-lucia.s: The United Workers Party is one of the two main political parties of Saint Lucia, founded in 1964 and led for decades by John Compton. It governed when Saint Lucia became an associated state of Britain in 1967 and led it to independence in 1979, with Compton as the first prime…

university-of-chicago.s: The University of Chicago is a private research university in Chicago, founded in 1890 with funding from John D. Rockefeller.

university-of-tubingen.s: The University of Tübingen was founded in 1477 by Count Eberhard V of Württemberg, called the Bearded, in his town of Tübingen. It became the university of the Duchy of Württemberg and, after the duchy adopted the Reformation in 1534, a centre of Lutheran theology.

upper-alsace.s: Upper Alsace is the southern part of Alsace, between the Vosges, the Rhine and the Swiss frontier, roughly the modern department of Haut-Rhin. In the Middle Ages much of it was held by the Habsburgs, while towns such as Colmar and Mulhouse were imperial cities and members of…

upper-austria.s: Upper Austria is a historical land of the Habsburg monarchy along the Danube west of the Enns river, with Linz as its capital, and is now one of Austria's federal states. Known in the Middle Ages as the land above the Enns, it gradually became a separate land from Lower Austria.

upper-hungary.s: Upper Hungary is the historical name for the northern part of the Kingdom of Hungary, roughly modern Slovakia and parts of north-eastern Hungary, with towns such as Kassa (Košice) and Pozsony (Bratislava). Its mining towns produced silver and gold.

upper-nubia.s: Upper Nubia is the southern part of Nubia, along the Nile in modern Sudan from the Second Cataract southwards. It was the heartland of Kush: the kingdom of Kerma flourished at the Third Cataract from about 2500 BCE, and later Napata and Meroë lay further upstream.

upper-swabia.s: Upper Swabia is the region of south-western Germany between the Danube, the Iller and Lake Constance, in modern Baden-Württemberg and Bavaria. In the Holy Roman Empire it was divided among many small territories, including imperial abbeys such as Weingarten, imperial cities…

uriah-butler.s: Tubal Uriah 'Buzz' Butler was a Grenadian-born labour leader and preacher in Trinidad. A former oilfield worker, he led the oilfield strike of June 1937, which spread into unrest across Trinidad and Tobago and led to the recognition of trade unions and labour reforms.

urien-rheged.s: Urien Rheged was a king of Rheged in northern Britain in the late 6th century, praised in poems attributed to Taliesin. The Historia Brittonum records him leading a coalition of British kings that besieged the Angles of Bernicia on Lindisfarne, before he was murdered at the…

urus-khan.s: Urus Khan was a Jochid ruler of the White Horde, in the eastern part of the Golden Horde, from about 1368 until his death in 1377. He sought to reunite the Golden Horde and briefly held its capital Sarai, but was challenged by Tokhtamysh, who was backed by Timur.

usatges-of-barcelona.s: The Usatges of Barcelona are a collection of customary laws of Catalonia, traditionally attributed to Count Ramon Berenguer I of Barcelona in the mid-11th century but largely compiled in the 12th. They dealt with feudal relations, the keeping of the peace and the authority of…

usman-zaki.s: Usman Zaki was the first emir of Bida in the Nupe country of central Nigeria. A son of the Fulani cleric Mallam Dendo, he became ruler of the Fulani-led Nupe state in the 1830s, was driven out by rivals and then restored with support from Gwandu around 1856, when Bida became…

uthman-dey.s: Uthman Dey was dey of Ottoman Tunisia from 1598 until his death in 1610, when deys chosen from the Janissary corps held real power. He organised the administration and the corsair fleet and welcomed Morisco refugees expelled from Spain from 1609, who founded towns and…
